summary.name: Akkoma
summary.one_liner: Akkoma is a federated microblogging server, a specialised fork of Pleroma, that lets users post, follow and react across the ActivityPub-based fediverse.
use_cases: Run a private or community social server for the fediverse
Communicate with Mastodon and Pleroma users from one account
Post formatted content with Misskey markdown
Migrate an existing Pleroma server to a faster fork
Use custom emoji reactions to respond to friends' posts
summary.what_it_does: Akkoma is a fediverse server that implements the ActivityPub protocol, so its users can follow and talk with accounts on Mastodon, Pleroma and other ActivityPub services. Features listed include posts with unlimited attachments, follows and lists, emoji reactions, Misskey-flavoured markdown, unlimited post edits, quote posts and polls. It can use the Mastodon web frontend. The page says it is 30-50% faster than Pleroma on common operations. Chats were removed by design and the maintainer says they will not be added back.
notable: Specialised fork of Pleroma that aligns more closely with Misskey
Misskey-flavoured markdown and custom emoji reactions
Migration from Pleroma supported, though rollback is harder
caveats: Real-time chats were removed and are not planned to return
Rolling back from Akkoma to Pleroma is harder and may cause data loss for features that differ
Users must choose an instance to join unless they host their own
